newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul to cap 1998 budget growth at about nine pct.
newsitem.headline: Seoul to cap 1998 budget growth at about nine pct.

text.p: South Korea will cap next year's budget growth at about nine percent, against a 13.4 percent rise in 1997 and 14.8 percent growth in 1996, the Finance and Economy Ministry said in a statement on Tuesday.
It said the ministry estimated next year's real economic growth at five to six percent, against an assumed 5.5 percent rise in 1997 and a 7.1 percent growth in 1996.
The ministry expected next year's consumer inflation, measured by the consumer price index growth, at between 4.0 and 4.5 percent, against a 4.5 percent growth in 1996, it said.
The nation's budget, including special accounts, has been set to increase to about 71 trillion won this year from 63 trillion won in 1996, it said.
The target of holding the budget growth to a single digit reflected the government's belt-tightening stance on economic policies, it said.

Last Thursday, Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik told a news conference the government would slash tax revenues and government spending by two trillion won this year as part of belt-tightening measures to keep inflation under control.
South Korea has forecast this year's current account deficit at about $18 billion, down from a record $23.72 billion shortfall in 1996.

A cyclical downturn in South Korea's key export industries, including semiconductors and ships, and the Japanese yen's steep depreciation against the U.S. dollar were blamed for the snowballing deficit.
The ministry statement said detailed budget guidelines for government ministries and organisations would be delivered on March 31 and draft applications would be received by May 31.
After reviewing applications, the ministry plans to submit its draft version to the cabinet council for approval in late September, the statement said.
A final government draft, approved by the cabinet council, will be sent to the National Assembly for screening and approval by December 2, it said.
